thread.title: ETF Preview: ETFs, Futures Point Lower as Turkey Tensions Linger, Street Focuses on Economic Data

author: MT Newswires
title: ETF Preview: ETFs, Futures Point Lower as Turkey Tensions Linger, Street Focuses on Economic Data
text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds ahead of Wednesday's regular session:
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): -2.9%
SPDR Select Sector Fund - Financial ( XLF ): -0.8%
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): -0.6%
iPath S&P 500 VIX ST Futures ETN ( VXX ): +5.1%
VanEck Vectors Gold Miners ETF ( GDX ): -1.5%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including IWM and IVV were lower. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ (QQQ) was down 0.8%.
US stock futures pointed to a lower open ahead of the release of a raft of readings on the US economy, while lingering concerns over the financial turmoil in Turkey also weighed on sentiment.
In economic data news, retail sales rose 0.5% for July, versus the expectations for a 0.1% increase. Excluding autos, retail sales for the month rose 0.6%. Meanwhile, the June gain was revised to an increase of 0.2% from the prior reading of 0.5%; excluding autos, the June increase was revised to 0.2% from 0.4%.
The Empire State general business conditions index showed a reading of 25.6 in August versus 22.6 in July and compared with forecasts for a reading of 20.0.
The Q2 productivity showed a preliminary reading of 2.9% gain, compared with the consensus for a preliminary estimate of a 2.5% gain. Preliminary unit labor costs declined 0.9% during Q2, versus consensus estimates for an increase of 0.5%.
Looking ahead, the July reading for industrial production will be out 9:15 am ET, with expectations for an increase of 0.3%; forecasts for manufacturing call for a rise of 0.3%.
At 10 am ET, business inventories for June are expected to have a build of 0.1% versus a 0.4% gain in May. Expectations for August's housing market index are another 68 vs 68 in the prior month.
Power Play: Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) was down 0.2% and other funds Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones US Consumer Goods (IYK) were flat.
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) was down 0.7% and retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT), PowerShares Dynamic Retail (PMR) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were inactive in pre-market trade.
Macy's Inc (M) shares fell more than 5% after the retailer said Q2 revenue was down year-over-year, comparable sales were flat and adjusted earnings beat analyst expectations. For fiscal Q2 ended Aug 4, the company's adjusted profit increased to $0.59 per share from $0.37 per share for the same quarter last year ending July 29 and beat the Capital IQ consensus estimate of $0.50 per share. On a reported basis, the company earned $0.53 per share. Total revenue fell 1.2% to $5.57 billion from $5.63 billion, but beat the estimated $5.55 billion. For 2018, the company raised its adjusted EPS guidance to $3.95-$4.15 from previous guidance of $3.75-$3.95, which is above estimates for $3.87 per share. Total sales, however, are expected to be flat to up 0.7%.
Winners and Losers
Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs ( XLF ) was down 0.6%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was down 1.7% and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) was down 1.5%.
Genworth Financial (GNW) and China Oceanwide Holdings said they have agreed to a sixth waiver and agreement of each party's right to terminate the companies' merger agreement. The latest agreement extends the previous deadline of Aug. 15 to Dec. 1 to allow additional time to complete regulatory reviews. The agreement also waives the unstacking of Genworth Life and Annuity Insurance from Genworth Life Insurance, regulatory approval of which had been a condition of Oceanwide's obligation to close the merger. It also waives each party's covenants with respect to the unstacking, including Oceanwide's obligation to contribute $525 million, and Oceanwide's obligation to contribute $600 million to Genworth for the repayment of debt. Separately, Oceanwide has agreed to contribute $1.5 billion to Genworth over time following the close of the merger, with the final amounts of the plan to be contributed by March 31, 2020. The contribution will be used to improve Genworth's financial stability, which may include retiring Genworth's debt due in 2020 and 2021 or enabling growth opportunities. GNW shares fell marginally in pre-market trade.
Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) was down 0.9% and other tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW), iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) and iShares S&P North American Technology-Software Index (IGV) were inactive.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) were both flat.
Apple (AAPL) shares were acquired in several transactions by Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.A, BRK.B) in Q2, according to a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. The company increased its stake in Apple by 12.4 million shares in the quarter, bringing its total holdings to $46.6 billion at the end of June. AAPL shares fell 0.6% in pre-market trade.
Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) was flat and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was down 0.8% in pre-market trade.
Enphase Energy (ENPH) fell some 6% after it said it has priced $60 million aggregate principal amount of convertible senior notes due 2023 in a private placement to qualified institutional buyers. The company also said that Thurman John Rodgers, an affiliate of the company who is a director and stockholder, agreed to purchase $5 million aggregate principal amount of convertible senior notes due 2023 in a concurrent private placement. The sale of the convertible notes to the initial purchasers is expected to settle on Aug. 17, and is expected to result in approximately $57.6 million in net proceeds to the company after deducting fees and estimated offering expenses payable by the company. The sale of the affiliate notes is also expected to settle on Aug. 17, and is expected to result in approximately $4.9 million in net proceeds to Enphase.
Commodities
Crude was down 1%. United States Oil Fund (USO) was down 1.4%. Natural gas was down 0.5% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was up 0.8%.
Gold was down 0.6%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was down 0.6%. Silver was down 1.8%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was down 1.5%.
Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) and other health care funds Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones US Healthcare (IYH) were inactive. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was down 0.4% in pre-market trading .
Pain Therapeutics (PTIE) rose nearly 29% after it said the National Institutes of Health (NIH) awarded the company a $3.2 million clinical research grant to support a phase II study with PTI-125, the company's drug candidate to treat Alzheimer's disease. Pain Therapeutics expects to initiate the study in Q4.
